text: What is a well-documented weakness of toxin-antitoxin kill-switch biocontainment systems in engineered organisms?
choices: They require continuous refrigeration to remain functional
They can legally only be used inside BSL-4 facilities
Evolution frequently inactivates the kill switch because there is strong selection against self-destruction
They increase the transmissibility of the host organism to other hosts
explanation: The chapter notes that evolution frequently inactivates kill switches, since any mutation disabling the toxin-antitoxin circuit is strongly selected for, undermining containment over time -- this is why multi-layered containment is recommended. Kill switches have no special refrigeration or BSL-4-only requirement, and they have nothing to do with increasing transmissibility, which is an unrelated DURC concern about pathogen enhancement.
